task: Escribe 80–100 palabras sobre un objetivo difícil que te propusiste (o que te gustaría proponerte): cómo empezaste, qué dificultades hubo y qué consejo darías. Usa used to, managed to.
paragraphs: Three years ago, Tom Hughes could not run for a bus. He was forty-five, he worked long hours in an office, and his only exercise was walking to the car. Then his doctor gave him a warning: his blood pressure was too high, and he needed to change his lifestyle.

Tom decided to try running, but he started very carefully. He downloaded a free beginners' programme that combined one minute of running with ninety seconds of walking, three times a week. "The first day, I thought I was going to die," he laughs. "After sixty seconds I was completely out of breath."

Little by little, the running periods got longer. After nine weeks, he could run for thirty minutes without stopping. He joined a local running club, where he met people of all ages and abilities. "Nobody cared how slow I was," he says. "They just cheered when I finished."

Encouraged by his new friends, Tom set himself a bigger goal: a full marathon, 42.2 kilometres. He trained for eight months, increasing the distance gradually and learning about rest, food and proper shoes. He also learned to listen to his body; when his knee started to hurt, he stopped for two weeks instead of ignoring the pain.

Last April, Tom crossed the finish line of the London Marathon in five hours and twelve minutes. "I wasn't fast, but I didn't walk once," he says proudly. His blood pressure is now normal, and he has lost fifteen kilos.
His advice for beginners? "Start slower than you think you need to, find people to run with, and celebrate small victories. Nobody becomes a runner in a week."
